value.value: By relaxing restrictive assumptions of earlier models, we show that sheltering promotes fixation of LOF mutations with sexually dimorphic fitness effects, resulting in decay of X-linked genes that are exclusively expressed by males and Y-linked genes that are primarily, though not necessarily exclusively, expressed by females.

fields.definition: Systems and conditions to which the claim applies, including explicit exclusions.

value.value: A population-genetic model of homologous X and Y regions that no longer recombine and start with the same functional genes; it applies equally to Z and W chromosomes with the sexes switched. It concerns loss-of-function mutations: fixation on the X requires complete recessivity, while incomplete recessivity narrows, but does not remove, gene loss from the Y. Its importance in nature depends on the distribution of dominance and of sex-specific fitness effects.

fields.definition: Observations the hypothesis accounts for. Each item records the observation, its current status (unexplained, contested, explained by a rival hypothesis, or explained by an accepted account), whether the hypothesis explains it directly or as a consequence, and the atoms or predictions that do the explaining. Only unexplained and contested observations count as gaps in knowledge. Serves the question: which gaps in knowledge would the hypothesis close if confirmed?
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary: status unexplained | contested | explained_by_rival | explained; mode direct | consequence
fields.example: Y-linked gene loss after recombination stops, explained by an accepted account

value.observation: After recombination stops between the X and Y, the Y loses genes.

fields.definition: Existing findings that the hypothesis reads differently: the finding, its current interpretation, the proposed interpretation and the atoms that ground it. Serves the question: which existing data would the hypothesis make us reinterpret?
fields.vocabulary: No fixed vocabulary; each item holds the finding, its current and proposed interpretations and the atom identifiers
fields.example: early models read as a rejection of sheltering, reread under sex-specific costs

value.finding: Early models showed that recessive lethal mutations stay rare on the Y in large populations, because the same mutations also arise on the X.
value.current_interpretation: Sheltering cannot cause Y-linked gene loss, so Muller's hypothesis is rejected.
value.proposed_interpretation: The models assumed lethal mutations with equal costs in both sexes. When costs differ between the sexes, sheltering fixes loss-of-function alleles on the X or the Y.

fields.definition: New questions that the hypothesis makes worth asking, why they are not asked today and, when known, the method that would answer them. Serves the question: which new directions would the hypothesis open?
fields.vocabulary: No fixed vocabulary; each item holds the question, why it could not be asked before, the enabling method and the atom identifiers
fields.example: whether ants spread bactericidal fatty acids by grooming

value.new_question: What is the full distribution of dominance of loss-of-function mutations, not only its mean?
value.why_not_askable_today: Most available mutation data were insufficient for estimating aspects of the distribution of dominance other than its mean.
value.enabling_method: Genetic engineering combined with high-throughput phenotyping.

fields.definition: Whether the claim can be tested in any system, in principle and in practice, with a justification and the cheapest known test. When a human study is the cheapest test, the test refers to profile.human_testability instead of restating it.
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary: in_principle testable | not_testable | unclear; in_practice feasible_now | needs_new_method | not_feasible | unclear
fields.example: testable and feasible now, cheapest test a chemical disruptor

value.justification: The model is formal; its predictions can be compared with the gene content and gene losses of sex chromosomes in taxa where the ancestral genes and their sex-specific functions are known. Its importance in nature also needs measurements of dominance and of sex-specific fitness costs, which are harder to obtain.

cheapest_test.text: In a taxon with known ancestral sex-chromosome genes, test whether Y-linked genes whose ancestral function mattered most for females decayed fastest.

fields.definition: When the idea was first proposed: a date at the stated precision, the record that shows it, and whether the date comes from the author's statement or from a bounded search. A bounded search names its search scope.
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary: precision year | month | day; basis author_statement | bounded_search

source_ref.limitation: The article itself; its full text is not in this repository.

value.note: The extension is proposed in this article (paragraph 5); the date is its electronic publication date. Muller's original sheltering hypothesis dates from 1914. The article also credits Neuhaus (1939) with the intuition that X-linked male-limited genes might decay, and builds on the model of Mrnjavac et al. (2023) (paragraph 45).

fields.definition: Author's narrative mechanism, separate from a verified causal conclusion.

value.value: Our model shows that sheltering of LOF mutations promotes the evolutionary decay of certain types of genes from X and Y chromosomes, resulting in enrichments of female-biased genes on the X (owing to a deficit of male-limited genes) and male-biased genes on the Y (owing to a deficit of genes that are more important for female than male fitness).

fields.definition: Persistent source identifier or unresolved source reference without fabrication.
Typed relation of this citation to the current assertion, distinct from biological causation.
Retained retrieval and inspection context distinguishing available material from material actually inspected.
fields.example: full text retrieved and inspected on 2026-01-01

fields.definition: Source-supported independent and failed replication evidence with an explicit assessment status.
fields.example: repeated once by an independent group with the same result

fields.definition: How far the evidence is from the claim it is attached to, judged separately for the test system, the endpoint, the intervention and the comparison: none, some, serious or not applicable. It is the assessment of whoever recorded it. It covers only the system, the endpoint, the intervention and the comparison; that a line cites data rather than reporting them is recorded in its independence group.
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary, not GRADE or RoB 2: a mapping to external schemes follows only after a check against their primary sources; none | some | serious | not_applicable
fields.example: system serious (mouse for human), endpoint none

fields.definition: Risk that the study behind the line is biased: low, some, high or not assessed, with an optional tool reference and note. It is the assessment of whoever recorded it.
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary, not GRADE or RoB 2: a mapping to external schemes follows only after a check against their primary sources; low | some | high | not_assessed

fields.definition: Lines with the same group label rest on the same data, study or laboratory and are not independent of each other. It records who observed: a line that cites observations of a named work has the group of that work, so a review of other work is not a further independent source. When the cited work is not named, the line keeps the document's own group.
Where the data of the group first appeared: the article, registry record or accession. Lines of two cards with the same key rest on the same data, whatever their labels.
fields.vocabulary: scheme doi | pmid | pmcid | registry | accession, and its identifier

fields.definition: Whether the line rests on observation or experiment (empirical), on a simulation, or on a mathematical derivation or proof. It is the kind of argument, not whose data it is: empirical: the line rests on observation or experiment, whether the document reports it or cites it. How far the line is from the data is recorded in its indirectness and independence group, not here.
How the evidence lines were selected: the queries run and the number of records identified, screened and included, with the reasons and counts for exclusions.
fields.vocabulary: OHF vocabulary: counts, not a PRISMA flow diagram

fields.definition: A record that was found for a target and not used as an evidence line, with the type of the mismatch, its quotation and where it stands; the counts stay in selection_record.
fields.vocabulary: reason from ohf:terms@1, exclusion_reason: species_mismatch | direction_mismatch | endpoint_mismatch | type_mismatch | inherited_mismatch | other (with a note)
fields.example: inherited_mismatch: a mouse finding against a claim about humans

fields.definition: Source-reported funding and conflict-of-interest declarations, distinguishing explicit absence from unreported information.
fields.example: funded by fund G; authors declare no competing interests

fields.definition: Author of the scientific content, separate from whoever entered the record and from any translator.

value.value: Andrea Mrnjavac, Beatriz Vicoso, Tim Connallon

fields.definition: Funding and conflict-of-interest declarations of the author whose claim the card records, as the source states them, distinguishing explicit absence from unreported information. A cited work's declarations are in evidence.references[].funding_coi.
fields.example: funded by fund G; author A is a consultant for company C

fields.definition: Declared author/agent kind without inferring legal identity.
fields.vocabulary: OHF agent vocabulary, with source declaration

fields.definition: Actual declared model and version used for generation or extraction, with attestation basis.
fields.vocabulary: Provider report or explicitly client-declared identity

fields.definition: How this claim arose, distinct from who authored it.
fields.vocabulary: OHF: de_novo, the claim is proposed in the work the card is made from and derives from no earlier hypothesis record, so it has no parent_refs (what inspired it goes in inspiration_refs); refine, the claim changes one earlier hypothesis, named in parent_refs, by narrowing, extending or correcting it; merge, the claim joins two or more earlier hypotheses, each named in parent_refs; import, the claim is taken over unchanged from a record of another registry or format; published_restatement, the card restates a claim that a published work already states, read from author.source. The value says how this record's claim arose, not who wrote it: the author of the source and the means of writing it are in author.generator

fields.definition: Author-declared method such as anomaly, analogy or screening.
fields.vocabulary: Method declared by the author, not inferred from writing style

fields.definition: Actual refinement/merge parents with versioned lineage and transformation scope.
Attributed inspirations; inspiration does not itself create a descendant relation.
fields.vocabulary: References to attributed sources of inspiration

fields.definition: What relevant data/results the author knew, with declaration time and scope.
fields.vocabulary: Source-bound declaration of what the author knew

fields.definition: Exact original bytes or retained artifact reference, encoding/media type and byte hash.
fields.vocabulary: OHF SHA-256 byte binding, not a Trusty URI
fields.example: source artifact A with hash supplied by ingestion

fields.definition: Field path, exact source artifact hash and locator for each extracted assertion.
Converter versions, prompt or configuration references, and explicit changes.
Original language/text, translated proposal and translator identity/basis.
Asset-specific licence/permission and conditions, distinct from source-site software licence.
fields.vocabulary: SPDX identifier only when verified, otherwise verbatim terms

fields.definition: Who created, curated, translated or reviewed each record and when.

Registration time and immutable record, distinct from assertion/source times. It records the registration of this hypothesis record itself; registrations of studies cited as evidence, such as trial registry entries, belong in evidence.references.
fields.vocabulary: Source-bound record of the registration event

fields.definition: Source-grounded heuristic principles used in the claim, with a pinned vocabulary and explicit justification.
fields.example: competing-explanations, justified by "We compared competing explanations"

value.basis_quote: We compared competing explanations for the rise in counter Y.

fields.definition: Author-stated form of the dose-response relation, not fitted from prose.
fields.vocabulary: Source wording, such as monotone; OHF 1.0 fixes no list

fields.definition: What varies along the curve: concentration, delivered dose or exposure, with units.
Endpoint and system whose response shape is claimed.
Dose range and conditions to which that shape applies.
Individual agents/doses and how their combination is administered.
Named reference expectation for the exact endpoint/system, with its assumptions and scale; reference models are not interchangeable additive formulas.
fields.vocabulary: Bliss, Loewe, HSA or ZIP when explicitly supplied

fields.definition: Observed or predicted combination contrast under that named model.

Repeatable attributed roles bound to an explicit readout/prediction reference and context of use; roles may include exposure, target engagement, mediator, prognostic marker, clock, surrogate or direct endpoint.
fields.vocabulary: Source wording of the role; OHF 1.0 fixes no list

fields.definition: Repeatable validation assessments bound to an explicit readout/prediction reference, target outcome, system/population and intervention context; validation cannot transfer between predictions by proximity.
Predicted or observed adverse effects with dose/system/time context and source.
Limits on transfer across sex, strain, species or human populations.
Function/process under discussion, with optional hallmarks mapping kept separate.
fields.vocabulary: Reviewed GO/Reactome mapping, no mandatory hallmarks ontology

fields.definition: Hallmarks of aging that atoms of this card concern, each with the atoms that concern it. A classification of the card, not a claim of the source; only in the aging profile.
fields.vocabulary: ohf:hallmarks@1: the twelve hallmarks of López-Otín et al. 2023

fields.definition: Source-supported human feasibility, ethical constraints, regulatory path and prerequisites, preserving unknown components.
fields.example: no human counterpart; no human study applies

fields.definition: Source-attributed scientific explanation/background kept separate from field extraction.
Detailed proposed experiment with design, sampling, controls and analysis plan.
fields.vocabulary: OSF/ARRIVE-informed plan, not a completed study

fields.definition: Lossless retained external sections that no card field represents.
fields.example: source Risk Factors and Limitations section

fields.definition: Author-stated limitations and separate curator commentary with clear attribution.
The two fixed hypothesis versions being related or compared.
Curated relation of claims, not forced mutual exclusivity.
fields.vocabulary: The relation types of ohf:hypothesis-relations@1: rival_same_explanandum | nested | compatible_independent | duplicate | refines | unrelated | analog | mechanism_neighbour

fields.definition: Whether a scoped observation could distinguish the pair, with assessor/reason.
Observation alternatives and each hypothesis's predicted result/likelihood, retaining unknowns.
fields.example: observation O favors A only if stated predictions differ

fields.definition: Proposed discriminating test with context, predictions and resolution rule.
Shared and differing assumptions needed to interpret the pair test.

Reference to the comparison context binding the pool, criterion version and protocol, together with the exact hypothesis versions and displayed-source/brief contracts. A question is optional claim context, not the comparison key.
fields.vocabulary: OHF pool / versioned criterion / protocol context
